title: Privacy notice says our websites run no analytics, but the admin site allows Cloudflare's visit counter
what: The privacy notice promises no cookies, no ads and no analytics on our websites. The admin site's security rules explicitly allow Cloudflare's visit-counter script, and the note beside it says Cloudflare adds it to the page. A visit counter is analytics.
expected: Either the notice names Cloudflare's cookie-free visit counter, or the counter is switched off on every site the notice covers.
how_often: every visit to the admin site, if Cloudflare's counter is on (whether it is on is set in Cloudflare, unknown here)
fix_line: Add one line to the notice naming Cloudflare's visit counter, or turn it off

title: Delete-your-account page promises the gym's records lose the member's number; the privacy notice says the gym decides
what: The delete-account page says that when a member leaves the gym in the app, their mobile number is erased from the gym's records. The privacy notice says only the app's link to the gym loses the number, and the gym decides about the rest. The two legal pages promise different things about the same personal data.
expected: Both pages say the same thing, and it matches what leaving the gym really does.
how_often: every member who reads either page
fix_line: Make the delete-account page use the privacy notice's narrower wording

title: Tapping an admin alert can bring the open tab forward without opening the alert's page
what: When an admin tab is already open, tapping a pop-up alert focuses that tab and tries to move it to the alert's page. The tab list also includes tabs the background helper does not control, and moving those fails; the failure only goes to the hidden log, so the owner sees whatever page was open, not the alert.
expected: The tap always lands on the page the alert names, for example by opening a new tab when moving the old one fails.
who: gym owners and staff using alerts
how_often: cannot be proven in the cloud, needs a real-phone check (an admin tab opened before the latest update, then tap an alert)
fix_line: When moving the open tab fails, open the alert's page in a new window

title: Admin alerts use the full-colour app picture as the small status-bar badge
what: The small status-bar badge on an admin alert is the same full-colour picture as the big icon, from a different folder than the installed app's icons. Android draws the badge as one colour only, so a full-colour square picture shows as a plain white blob.
expected: A one-colour outline badge of the current brand mark, from the same brand folder as the app icons.
who: gym owners and staff on Android
how_often: cannot be proven in the cloud, needs a real-phone check (look at the status bar after a test alert)
fix_line: Add a one-colour badge picture and point the alert at it

title: Privacy notice says a page keeps only the light or dark choice, but the join page keeps the visitor's name and number
what: The notice says a page may remember only the light or dark choice on the device. The Become-a-member page keeps the language choice, and keeps the typed name and mobile number in the browser until the tab closes.
expected: The notice says the join page keeps the form answers on the device until the tab is closed, or the page stops keeping them.
fix_line: Widen the notice line to cover form answers and language

title: A brand-new install shows 'new feature' dots on things that are not new to that member
what: The What's new card is never shown to a fresh install, because nothing is new to them. The new-feature dots do not follow that rule: on a fresh install the seen list is empty, so every feature released in the last 30 days lights dots on the Profile tab, the Settings button and the Settings rows, up to 3 at once.
expected: A fresh install starts with every current feature already counted as seen, the same way What's new treats it.
who: members who install the app for the first time
how_often: every fresh install within 30 days of a feature release
fix_line: On first launch, mark every feature already in the app as seen

title: The MettleUp team's answer to a help question rides on the gym-messages pop-up channel
what: When the team answers a member's help question, the phone's pop-up goes on the 'Messages from your gym' channel. A member who turned that channel off, or who is on an iPhone, gets no pop-up and nothing tells them why; they only see a red dot if they open the app. The pop-up is also skipped silently when notifications are not allowed.
expected: The team's answer has its own channel (or the help screen says replies only pop up when gym messages are on), and an iPhone member is told to check back.
how_often: cannot be proven in the cloud, needs a real-phone check (turn off the gym-messages channel in Android settings, then get a reply)
fix_line: Give the team's replies their own pop-up channel

title: The watch screen log sends a little more than its caption and the privacy notice say
what: The switch caption and the privacy notice say the watch screen log holds only the screen on, off and dim times and the Battery Saver and screen settings. It also sends whether a workout was open at each moment, the watch app's version, and the last update pop-up decision.
expected: The caption and notice name everything the log carries, or the log sends only what they name.
who: members with a watch who send feedback
how_often: every time the switch is used
fix_line: Add 'whether a workout was open and the watch app version' to the caption and notice

title: The 'Cancel receipt' button stays grey with no reason shown
what: The button that cancels a receipt is greyed out until the reason box holds a minimum number of letters. The screen never says how long the reason must be; the message that would say so can only appear after pressing the button, which cannot be pressed while it is grey.
expected: Next to the reason box, the screen says the reason needs at least that many letters, or the button stays pressable and shows the message.
how_often: every time someone types a short reason
fix_line: Say the minimum length in the reason box's hint

title: Cancelling a receipt that was paid online says nothing about the money held by the payment company
what: Online payments save a receipt marked 'Paid online' with the payment company's reference. The cancel-receipt screen treats it like cash: it says the money no longer counts and adds it back to the member's dues. It does not say the member really paid through the payment company, or that a refund there is a separate step, so the member can be chased for money they already paid.
expected: For an online-paid receipt, the screen says the money is still with the gym's payment company and asks whether it was refunded there before adding it back to dues.
who: gym owners using online payments, and their members
how_often: every time an online-paid receipt is cancelled
fix_line: Show a refund warning when the receipt was paid online

title: Freeze / extra days does not mention a next plan already sold
what: The freeze screen pushes a plan's last day later and shows the new last day. It never looks at a renewal already sold to start the day after the old last day. The change-start screen does check for clashes with the member's other plans; this one does not, so the screen does not say whether the freeze days overlap the next plan. Whether the save step moves the next plan was not in this folder (unknown).
expected: When a next plan is already sold, the screen says the freeze days push that plan later too (or warns they overlap).
who: gym owners, members who renewed early and then freeze
how_often: every freeze on a member who has already renewed
fix_line: Pass the member's other plans to the freeze screen and say what happens to the next one

title: 'Continue with your phone number' lives only on the first-run welcome
what: Phone-number sign-in (which finds the member's own gym and role) is a button on the welcome screen. The welcome screen shows only when no profile exists on the phone, so a member or trainer who set up the app before the switch went on never sees it. No other way into it is in this folder; whether another screen offers it is unknown.
expected: Existing users get the same check from Settings or the Gym tab.
who: members and trainers who installed before the switch
how_often: every existing user, once the switch is on
fix_line: Offer the phone check from Settings for people already set up

title: The phone sign-in box cuts a number longer than 16 characters
what: The phone sign-in number box takes at most 16 characters; the welcome step's own number box takes 24. A number pasted or autofilled with brackets or extra spaces, such as '+91 (98765) 43210', is cut short and then refused as not 10 digits.
expected: Both boxes allow the same room (24) and let the cleaning step remove spaces and signs.
who: members signing in with their number
how_often: cannot be proven in the cloud, needs a real-phone check (autofill and paste a spaced number)

title: The gym's public page takes names, numbers and chat questions the privacy notice does not mention
what: The gym's public page (hidden until switched on) asks visitors for name, mobile number and a question, and has a chat whose questions go to a server. The privacy notice's websites section names only the demo form and the friend invite page.
expected: Before the gym page is switched on, the notice says what the page collects, who gets it and how long it is kept.
who: visitors to a gym's public page
how_often: every visitor once the page is switched on
fix_line: Add the gym page to the privacy notice before switching it on
